content.text:
we have one persona that we are shipping by default For every egma customer right now what exactly is the prompt that goes inside the simulator when the persona is kind of speaking with the customer's agent? What exactly goes inside? Can you explain the whole thing to me through a flowchart or something like that? 

Also what is the llm that is being used and stuff like that for that default persona? I want to exactly understand how a persona works

The core answer: the Default Persona is one shared, read-only Egma persona. It is not copied for each customer. Its system prompt combines: 1. A fixed Egma instruction. 2. The Default Persona’s traits. 3. The current test’s scenario. 4. The full conversation history. This is exact for current `origin/main`, commit `e68cb90ce2f03bef95561718917d183e39e0aaa9`. I did not inspect the hosted deployment, so this does not prove which commit its containers run. ## The complete flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["One shared Default Persona v1"] --> B["New project points to it"] B --> C{"Does the test name personas?"} C -- "No" --> D["Test version saves the project's default persona ID"] C -- "Yes" --> E["Test version saves the selected persona IDs"] D --> F["Run pins the current persona version"] E --> F F --> G["Claim API builds SimulationSpec v3:
traits + models + test scenario + current provider keys"] G --> H["Simulator builds the system prompt"] H --> I{"Has the customer agent spoken?"} I -- "Yes" --> J["Add agent words as role: user"] I -- "No" --> K["Add hidden opening nudge as role: user"] J --> L["OpenAI gpt-4o-mini
system prompt + full history"] K --> L L --> M["Persona reply"] M --> N{"Contains [CONCLUDED]?"} N -- "No" --> O{"Chat or voice?"} O -- "Chat" --> P["Send text to the customer agent"] O -- "Voice" --> Q["Cartesia turns text into audio"] P --> R["Customer agent answers"] Q --> S["OpenAI STT turns agent audio into text"] R --> T["Append both turns to history"] S --> T T --> L N -- "Yes" --> U["Remove marker and end"] U --> V["Store turns and timing spans"] V --> W["Finish simulation and create grading work"] ``` I refreshed Graphify for this checkout: 1,069 code files, 11,284 nodes, and 28,876 post-cluster edges. Its queries centered on `projectDefaultPersona`, `resolvePersonaVersions`, `assembledSpec`, `RunningSimulation`, `Persona`, and `messages_for`. The API-to-simulator step crosses a JSON contract, so I checked both ends directly in the source. [Open the fresh Graphify call-flow export](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/visualizations/2026/08/25/01a03642-a2bb-74d3-9510-3c7ae83c3f8c/egma-persona/egma-persona-callflow.html) ## The exact system prompt Only the marked test scenario changes: ```text You are playing a person in a live conversation with a customer service agent. You are the person; the agent is who you are talking to. Who you are, exactly as authored: { "accent": "Neutral American English.", "backgroundNoise": "None.", "language": "en-US", "manner": "Clear, natural, and conversational.", "patience": "Starts patient and gives the agent time to explain.", "personality": "Speaks clear, natural English. Starts patient and cooperative, answers one question at a time, and becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive without becoming rude.", "underFriction": "Becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive, without becoming rude." } Why you are here today: How to conduct yourself: - Stay in character as this person for the whole exchange. Never mention being simulated, tested, or an AI. - Speak one conversational turn at a time, in plain spoken words — no lists, no headings, no stage directions. - Pursue what you came for until it is concluded to your satisfaction, and let your persona decide how patiently. - When your goal is concluded and nothing further is needed, say a brief goodbye and end your reply with [CONCLUDED]. ``` The exact template and role mapping are in [persona.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/persona.py:24). The exact Default Persona traits are in [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54). There is no single universal final prompt because every test supplies a different scenario. ## What is sent to the LLM If the customer agent has not spoken, the first request has this shape: ```json { "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "" }, { "role": "user", "content": "(The conversation is open and the agent is listening. Speak your first turn.)" } ] } ``` If the customer agent greets first, its greeting replaces that hidden nudge. On later calls: - Customer-agent turns use `role: "user"`. - Persona turns use `role: "assistant"`. - Egma sends the complete accumulated history each time. - The hidden opening nudge is not stored as a transcript turn. Egma sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`. The body contains only `model` and `messages`. Egma does not set temperature, token limits, tools, seed, `top_p`, or penalties. The timeout is 60 seconds. See [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:179). ## Exact models for Default Persona v1 | Function | Exact selection | |---|---| | Persona LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` | | Voice transcription | OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` | | Text-to-speech | Cartesia `sonic-3.5` | | Cartesia voice ID | `5ee9feff-1265-424a-9d7f-8e4d431a12c7` | | Speaking speed | `1` | | Voice activity detection | Silero in shipped Docker Compose; this is deployment configuration, not persona content | The repository has no human-readable name for that Cartesia voice ID. Chat simulations use only the LLM. Voice simulations use the same LLM plus OpenAI realtime transcription and Cartesia speech. The selections come from the immutable persona version; there is no simulator model or voice fallback. See [model catalog](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24) and [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:413). Provider keys are separate from the persona. For each simulation, the API loads the current OpenAI and Cartesia keys from AWS Secrets Manager in Egma Cloud, or from environment variables in self-hosted Egma. Missing keys cause a failure; Egma does not silently select another provider. ## What “default for every customer” really means - Every new project initially points to this one shared persona ID: `prs_01M0E4EVJ6ECGVJEA4NSBTC0CC`. - The migration gave it only to existing projects that had no default. It preserved existing custom choices. - A project admin can choose another default persona. - A test can explicitly name another persona. - A test that names no persona saves the project’s current default persona identity. - Starting a run pins the exact persona version used by that run. Therefore, the Default Persona is available to every project and is the initial default. It is not forced into every test forever. See [project provisioning](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/provisioning.ts:52), [test resolution](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/tests.ts:672), and [run pinning](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/runs.ts:704). The persona LLM does not receive expected behaviors, grader instructions, project or organization names, customer-agent configuration, connection credentials, mock tools, model settings, voice ID, or recordings. Grading happens afterward as a separate process. One current difference is worth knowing: voice speaks the final goodbye after removing `[CONCLUDED]`. Chat records that final goodbye but ends before sending it to the customer agent. Focused verification passed: 26 simulator tests and 11 TypeScript model-contract tests, 37 tests total. rollout_summaries/2026-08-20T03-58-26-16HI-egma_monitoring_audit_planning_context_git_state_and_thread.md:37-51|note=[used prior Graphify location and completion requirements] MEMORY.md:1484-1512|note=[used prior Graphify workflow guidance] MEMORY.md:1452-1474|note=[used historical persona cutover context and reverified it on current main] 01a01d51-f8e8-7473-80d1-d656ce1bc646 01a01b6d-317e-7b03-870f-00931b4d5841

content.text: I found the main cause. One Terra change was merged, but it used the old deployment-wide settings path. A later merged cutover removed that path and intentionally made persona versions the owner, seeding `gpt-4o-mini`. A newer Terra implementation exists, but it is still uncommitted in another worktree; no remote branch or pull request contains it. I’m now checking whether that unfinished implementation changes persona history safely.

The model did not silently revert. One merged design change replaced Terra with `gpt-4o-mini`, and the later Terra implementation never reached GitHub.

### Attempts and history

| Date | Attempt | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-15 | [PR #116](https://github.com/egma-ai/egma/pull/116), merge `7a095271`; commits `a324b55`, `471dc68` | Merged Terra with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. This used the old deployment/platform-setting path: `EGMA_PERSONA_MODEL`, `EGMA_PERSONA_MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`, API config, contract v1, and simulator environment fallback. The shared Default Persona did not exist yet. |
| 2026-08-20 | [PR #158](https://github.com/egma-ai/egma/pull/158), squash `4ead218` | Merged the persona-version ownership cutover. It deleted all model-choice environment/platform settings and reasoning support, created the shared Default Persona v1 with `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, constrained the DB, contract, and simulator to that pair, and deleted the old platform rows. This was not an explicit revert commit; it was a replacement architecture after a production mixed-setting failure. |
| 2026-08-21 | Stash `3d131746`; orphan untracked commit `59c7b1dd` | A substantial Terra implementation was written but never committed to a branch or pushed. It remains staged/untracked in `/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8927/egma`. No remote branch tip contains Terra, and GitHub search finds only PR #116. The branch’s PR #164 had already merged before this work. |

Current remote `main` is `d1dbbc759adfdc30aa546056a995e40bdd4162eb`, and the controlling catalog files have stayed on 4o-mini since PR #158.

### Exact root cause

PR #158 made code plus Postgres the source of truth:

- [model catalog](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24) supports only `gpt-4o-mini`.
- [Default Persona catalog](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:50) defines immutable v1 using that model.
- [database constraint](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/packages/db/src/schema/personas.ts:180) accepts only that LLM shape.
- [simulation contract](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/packages/simulation-contract/schemas/simulation-spec.v3.schema.json:203) accepts only that model.
- [simulator adapter](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:224) refuses every other LLM.
- API boot [reconciles the code catalog into Postgres](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/c93a/egma/apps/api/src/index.ts:86).

Current source contains no model-choice environment variable. Environment and AWS Secrets Manager provide credentials only: `EGMA_OPENAI_API_KEY`, or the current `openai_api_key` in the AWS provider bundle. They do not select the model.

### Problem with the unfinished attempt

The unfinished migration [0040_default_persona_terra.sql](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8927/egma/packages/db/migrations/0040_default_persona_terra.sql:1) drops the immutability trigger, rewrites Default Persona v1 in place, then restores the trigger.

That is unsafe and contradicts the domain contract:

- Old simulations pin v1 and must retain its original meaning.
- The catalog explicitly says a model change adds a new version.
- The DB guard says authored version content cannot change.
- The existing seeding test already proves the correct v2 flow.
- Its migration number also collides with migrations already on current `main`.
- It changes simulation contract v3 in place. Old workers also advertise v3, so the API could send them a new v3 document they cannot parse.

Do not commit that migration as written.

### Correct implementation

Create Default Persona v2:

1. Keep v1 unchanged with `gpt-4o-mini`.
2. Add `gpt-5.6-terra` to the LLM catalog with required `reasoningEffort: "none"`.
3. Add a new fixed `prsv_` ID as Default Persona version 2, with identical traits and:
   ```json
   {
     "provider": "openai",
     "model": "gpt-5.6-terra",
     "reasoningEffort": "none"
   }
   ```
4. Widen the Postgres constraint in the next migration after current `main`; never update v1 or disable its immutability guard.
5. Let the existing catalog seeder insert v2 and move the shared persona’s `current_version_id`. Projects still pointing at the shared Default Persona will use v2 on future runs. Old runs remain pinned to v1. Custom defaults and existing forks remain unchanged.
6. Create simulation contract v4, not a changed v3. Update the API contract constant and simulator schema filename so old v3 workers refuse claims through the existing version negotiation.
7. Carry `reasoningEffort` through the DB/public API as camel case, emit `reasoning_effort: "none"` on the simulator work order, parse it in Python, and send it on the OpenAI request.
8. Update the persona API/UI types and generated platform API if Terra should appear as an authorable model.
9. Prove the exact OpenAI request against the real account, then deploy and run one real Chat and one real Voice simulation.

The unfinished work identifies most affected files, but it must be rebuilt from current `main` with the v2 and contract-v4 corrections. I made no edits; the modified `persona.py` in this task and the Terra worktree changes both pre-existed my inspection.
